subject: Close runway: proposed stretch + acceptance path
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close runway: proposed stretch + acceptance path

Dana — thanks again for the catch on the integration window. I reviewed the MAP and eval cadence; looks like the critical path is the last acceptance gate (integration smoke + performance eval) which is now slipping by ~10 business days given your infra team’s bandwidth.

I attached an updated MAP (ACME_MAP_v3.docx) and a short risk log with suggested mitigations. Proposed approach:
- Stretch the go-live window by 10 business days to preserve a clean acceptance gate (minimize scope drift)
- Introduce a hard cutover readiness checklist we can run in parallel with the last two sprints
- Create a temporary SLA/rollback contingency (we can offer a one-week extended support window post-go-live)

If you’re OK, I’ll circulate the acceptance checklist and a DocuSign agreement to reflect the MAP update/extended-support commitment.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v3.docx, Close_Runway_Risk_Log.xlsx

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close runway: proposed stretch + acceptance path

Hi Chloe — appreciate the heads-up and the MAP refresh. Short version: our infra lead flagged two blockers that are the real cause of the 10-day drift:
1) A/V upgrade schedule conflict (cannot spin up the staging cluster until Apr 6)
2) Security needs a deeper SOC2 evidence extraction for the new telemetry stream (they requested the SOC2_subset.pdf)

Procurement also requested we minimize any contract changes; they asked for a single signature flow if the MAP edits are minor.

Can you send the specific acceptance checklist items we’ll run in parallel? If we can keep the changes narrowly scoped (no pricing changes) procurement will sign quickly.

—Dana Liu
Product Manager, Integrations | Acme Corp
Dana.Liu@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Close runway: proposed stretch + acceptance path

Chloe — thanks for looping us in. Two pragmatic mitigations to keep this from becoming a multi-week scramble:
1) Split acceptance into two discrete gates: 
   a) Integration smoke + regression (must pass before we schedule final performance run)
   b) Performance SLO validation (can be scheduled with a hard window once the staging cluster is available)
   This reduces risk of a full slip if smoke/regression can complete earlier.
2) Offer a one-week post-go-live enhanced support commitment (no additional cost) to cover any leftover verification items.

I updated the Close_Runway_Risk_Log.xlsx with these options and marked which items are gating vs advisory. Naomi — can you confirm we have available SRE hours to stand up the performance run if Acme's staging cluster comes up on Apr 6?

—Marissa
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Close runway: proposed stretch + acceptance path

We can commit a 2-person SRE slot for the performance run starting Apr 7 if the cluster is up. I added resource windows to the risk log and a tentative runbook (low/medium/high severity actions).

Note: if security’s SOC2 request delays the evidence handoff beyond Apr 2 we will need to shift the performance run one week; procurement constraints mean the DocuSign must reflect only the MAP timing change and the temporary support addendum — no pricing changes.

—Naomi
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme.com>, Tom Baker <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Updated MAP + acceptance checklist (requesting sign-off)

Dana / Tom — thanks for the quick coordination. Attached is the slimmed MAP (ACME_MAP_v3.docx) and the acceptance checklist excerpt. Summary of changes we are asking Acme to sign: 
- Official close date moved from Apr 15 to Apr 29 (10 business days extension)
- Acceptance split into: integration smoke/regression (target Apr 12–16) + performance SLO validation (Apr 20–23)
- Redwood to provide one-week enhanced support post-go-live (no charge)
- DocuSign prepared to reflect only these timing/support edits (no pricing/term changes): https://www.docusign.com/track/ABC-ACME-189

If procurement signs the DocuSign by EOD Mon (Apr 5), we will gate the performance run for Apr 7 and keep the Apr 29 close. If SOC2 evidence delivery pushes beyond Apr 2 we’ll need to rebaseline again — I included a short contingency lane in the risk log for that case.

Please reply with either: 1) sign-off, or 2) a single inline redline indicating the one item you cannot accept. I’ll coordinate legal for a clean signature flow if needed.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v3.docx, SOC2_subset.pdf, Close_Runway_Risk_Log.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to a quick decision so we can lock the MAP.

—Chloe
